title: The chat server's mutual-TLS control connection to the media server
spec: docs/CALLS.md 'Admission' and the control-channel decision of 2026-11-26. crewcraft_proto::media_control: DropPerson (kind 1: u64 seq | u64 call | str person, 1 to 320 bytes), EndCall (kind 2: u64 seq | u64 call), Ack (kind 128: u64 seq), each one frame. The media server binary moves to apps/crewcraft-media-server (crewcraft-media stays the pure-Rust media path); media.toml gains an optional [control] (listen, certificate, owner-only key, chat-server-ca: plain file names). ControlListener accepts TLS 1.3 with a client certificate that must chain to chat-server-ca (crewcraft-tls), at most 4 connections, feeds each message to the serving loop through intake::Handle and acknowledges it. The chat server reads media.toml in its data directory (server-name, address, control, key, ca-bundle, client-certificate, client-key; strict, files owner-only where secret); the media key is made at the first start (owner-only) with key.pub (64 hex characters) beside it; the server announces FEATURE_MEDIA and runs MediaLink beside the listener: every 50 ms it sweeps the calls, takes the MediaEvents and sends each until acknowledged, reconnecting after a second and resending what was not acknowledged. Test: both servers on loopback, two str0m clients over real UDP with credentials from the chat server: removing one from the room closes their media session within three seconds, the call's end closes the other, a client certificate from another CA gets no answer and drops no one; the chat server's media.toml is strict, missing means no media, the key is made once and kept, and a client key others can read is refused; the binary exits 2 without arguments and 1 naming a bad key.
